title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ecclesiastes chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ecclesiastes Chapter 5.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 5, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God
Be not rash with thy mouth
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it
For a dream cometh through the multitude of business
questions.correctAnswer: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:1 contains the command to keep thy foot when going to the house of God, which is the first instruction in the chapter.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 5, what should one be more ready to do than to give the sacrifice of fools?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:1 instructs to be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools.

questions.question: What does the fool's voice get known by, according to Ecclesiastes 5?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:3 states that a fool's voice is known by multitude of words.

questions.question: Where is God said to be located in Ecclesiastes 5?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:2 states that God is in heaven.

questions.question: What must one do when making a vow unto God as stated in Ecclesiastes 5?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:4 commands not to defer to pay a vow made unto God.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 5, who hath no pleasure in fools?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:4 says God hath no pleasure in fools.

questions.question: What is better than making a vow and not paying it, according to Ecclesiastes 5?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:5 states it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay.

questions.question: What should one not let their mouth cause, according to Ecclesiastes 5?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:6 instructs not to suffer thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin.

questions.question: Before whom should one not say it was an error, according to Ecclesiastes 5?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:6 warns not to say before the angel that it was an error.

questions.question: What is the consequence mentioned in Ecclesiastes 5 for causing God's anger at thy voice?
options: Destroy the work of thine hands
questions.correctAnswer: Destroy the work of thine hands
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:6 states God may be angry at thy voice and destroy the work of thine hands.

questions.question: What should one fear according to Ecclesiastes 5?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:7 concludes with the instruction to fear God.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5 says that God is upon earth.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:2 says God is in heaven, and thou upon earth, so God is not upon earth.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5 states that a multitude of dreams and many words contain divers vanities.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:7 states that in the multitude of dreams and many words there are also divers vanities.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5 says that it is better to vow and not pay than not to vow at all.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:5 states it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5 teaches that one should be quick and numerous in words before God.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:2 teaches to let thy words be few and not be rash or hasty to utter before God.

medium.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 5:8, why should one not marvel at the oppression of the poor and the perverting of judgment in a province?
options: Because there be higher than the highest who regard it
Because God does not see what happens on earth
Because the poor deserve their oppression
Because it is common in every province
questions.correctAnswer: Because there be higher than the highest who regard it
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:8 explains that one should not marvel at oppression because 'he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.'

questions.question: What promise does Ecclesiastes 5:9 give if one recognizes the profit of the earth?
options: The king himself is served by the field
The poor will be oppressed no more
Silver will satisfy the lover of silver
questions.correctAnswer: The king himself is served by the field
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:9 states 'Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field,' showing the provision of the earth benefits all, including the king.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 5:10 teach about the love of silver and abundance?
options: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase
Silver and abundance always satisfy the owner
Loving abundance brings great joy and peace
Silver is more valuable than gold
questions.correctAnswer: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:10 warns that loving silver and abundance does not satisfy, marking it as vanity.

questions.question: How do Ecclesiastes 5:11 and 5:12 together describe the effect of goods and riches on people?
options: Increase in goods leads to increased consumers, but the labourer's sleep is sweet unlike the rich who lose sleep
Goods increase only benefits the rich, and everyone sleeps well
The abundance of goods guarantees peaceful sleep for all
Riches cause happiness and restful sleep for everyone
questions.correctAnswer: Increase in goods leads to increased consumers, but the labourer's sleep is sweet unlike the rich who lose sleep
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:11 explains goods increase consumers, and 5:12 contrasts the sweet sleep of laborers with the restless sleep of the rich.

questions.question: What practical warning does Ecclesiastes 5:13 give regarding riches?
options: Riches kept for their owners can cause hurt
questions.correctAnswer: Riches kept for their owners can cause hurt
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:13 calls riches kept for owners 'a sore evil' to their hurt.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 5:14, what happens to riches that perish by evil travail?
options: They leave nothing in the hand of the son
They bring honor to the family
They are safely stored for heirs
questions.correctAnswer: They leave nothing in the hand of the son
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:14 explains that riches perishing by evil travail leave the son with nothing.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 5:1 advise regarding behavior when going to the house of God?
options: Be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools
Speak loudly and with many words
questions.correctAnswer: Be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:1 instructs to keep thy foot and be more ready to hear than to offer foolish sacrifices.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 5:2 emphasize the attitude of speech before God?
options: Let your words be few and avoid rashness
Speak many words to be heard
questions.correctAnswer: Let your words be few and avoid rashness
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:2 advises not to be rash and to let words be few before God.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 5:4 command about vows made to God?
options: Do not defer to pay what you vowed
Vows can be ignored if inconvenient
Vows should be made quickly and without thought
questions.correctAnswer: Do not defer to pay what you vowed
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:4 commands to pay what one has vowed without delay.

questions.question: What is better according to Ecclesiastes 5:5: to vow and not pay, or not to vow at all?
options: Better not to vow than to vow and not pay
Better to vow and not pay
questions.correctAnswer: Better not to vow than to vow and not pay
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:5 states it is better not to vow than to vow and not fulfill it.

questions.question: Why does Ecclesiastes 5:6 warn against causing the flesh to sin with the mouth before the angel?
options: Because God may be angry and destroy the work of your hands
questions.correctAnswer: Because God may be angry and destroy the work of your hands
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:6 warns that rash words can anger God and destroy your work.

questions.question: What is the main teaching of Ecclesiastes 5:7 regarding many words and dreams?
options: There are many vanities, but fear God
questions.correctAnswer: There are many vanities, but fear God
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:7 teaches that many words and dreams contain vanities, so one should fear God.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5:12 states that the abundance of the rich allows them to sleep well.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:12 states the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep, so it is false that it allows them to sleep well.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5:13 calls riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt a sore evil.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:13 explicitly calls this situation a sore evil under the sun.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5:14 says that riches perish by good travail and leave a son with much in his hand.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:14 states riches perish by evil travail and the son is left with nothing, so this statement is false.

hard.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ecclesiastes Chapter 5.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 5:15 state about a man's return after death?
options: He shall take nothing of his labour
He shall take all his riches
questions.correctAnswer: He shall take nothing of his labour
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ecclesiastes 5:15, which emphasizes that a man returns from where he came, taking nothing with him.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 5:16, what is considered a sore evil?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:16 presents the idea that laboring without meaningful gain is a serious problem.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 5:17 say about a man's experience of life?
questions.explanation: In Ecclesiastes 5:17, it is stated that a man's days are filled with sorrow and he eats in darkness.

questions.question: What is described as a gift from God in Ecclesiastes 5:19?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:19 indicates that the ability to enjoy one's labor is a gift from God.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 5:20, how will a man remember the days of his life?
options: He shall not much remember them
questions.correctAnswer: He shall not much remember them
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:20 states that a man will not remember his days significantly because God fills his heart with joy.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'labour' in Ecclesiastes 5:19 refer to?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'labour' in Ecclesiastes 5:19 refers to 'work', emphasizing the effort put into one's life.

questions.question: Which literary device is primarily used in Ecclesiastes 5:15–16?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:15–16 uses parallelism to compare a man's beginning and end, highlighting the transient nature of life.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of the futility of riches in Ecclesiastes 5:16?
questions.explanation: Luke 12:15 warns against coveting possessions, echoing Ecclesiastes 5:16's theme of laboring for the wind.

questions.question: Which other passage reflects on the fleeting nature of life, similar to Ecclesiastes 5:15?
questions.explanation: Psalm 39:5 reflects on the brevity of life, similar to the message in Ecclesiastes 5:15 about returning naked.

questions.question: What comes before Ecclesiastes 5:18?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:17 directly precedes 5:18, discussing a man's sorrow and darkness.

questions.question: What follows Ecclesiastes 5:20?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:1 follows 5:20, continuing the discourse on the themes of life and satisfaction.

questions.question: The Hebrew word 'evil' in Ecclesiastes 5:16 refers to which concept?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'evil' in Ecclesiastes 5:16 can denote 'misfortune', relating to the futility of labor without gain.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 5:19, what does 'portion' imply about God's gifts?
questions.explanation: The term 'portion' in Ecclesiastes 5:19 implies that God's gifts bring satisfaction and joy in one's labor.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5:18 suggests that enjoyment of life is futile.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:18 states that it is good to enjoy the labor one performs, indicating that enjoyment is not futile.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 5:20 implies that a man will often remember his days of life.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:20 states he shall not much remember the days of his life, indicating a lack of focus on the past.

theological.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ecclesiastes Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ecclesiastes 5:2 teach about the proper human posture before God?
options: Humans must speak sparingly and reverently before God due to His exalted position
God requires lengthy prayers and many words from worshippers
Human words have equal authority as God's decrees
God is indifferent to how humans approach Him verbally
questions.correctAnswer: Humans must speak sparingly and reverently before God due to His exalted position
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:2 instructs that one should not be rash or hasty in speech before God, emphasizing God's heavenly exaltation and human earthly status, thus teaching reverence and restraint in speech.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin is highlighted in Ecclesiastes 5:6?
options: Human speech can cause sin and provoke God's anger, affecting one's work
Sin is primarily a matter of external actions without internal consequences
God overlooks human verbal errors and does not punish speech
Sinful speech has no impact on divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Human speech can cause sin and provoke God's anger, affecting one's work
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:6 warns against letting the mouth cause the flesh to sin, highlighting that careless words can bring God's anger and destroy the work of one’s hands.

questions.question: What doctrine about the vanity of wealth is taught in Ecclesiastes 5:10?
options: Love of silver and abundance leads to perpetual dissatisfaction
Wealth guarantees lasting contentment and peace
Abundance increases joy and fulfills human desires permanently
Silver and riches are the ultimate goal ordained by God
questions.correctAnswer: Love of silver and abundance leads to perpetual dissatisfaction
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:10 reveals that those who love silver or abundance are never satisfied, teaching the futility and vanity in pursuing wealth as an end.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ecclesiastes 5:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:8 shows that God is 'higher than the highest' and watches over injustice, demonstrating His sovereign rule over earthly authorities.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Ecclesiastes 5:19 in relation to human enjoyment of labor?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:19 teaches that God gives riches, power, and the ability to enjoy the fruits of labor as a gift, highlighting His providential care.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 5:15 connect to the broader biblical theme of human mortality and stewardship?
options: It affirms that humans come into the world with nothing and leave with nothing, emphasizing stewardship over possessions
It encourages hoarding wealth for future generations
It portrays death as a transition to greater material gain
It denies human mortality by suggesting possessions are eternal
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that humans come into the world with nothing and leave with nothing, emphasizing stewardship over possessions
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:15 teaches that man enters and leaves life naked, reinforcing biblical themes like those in Job 1:21 about stewardship rather than ownership of material goods.

questions.question: In what way does Ecclesiastes 5:18-20 prepare for New Testament teachings about contentment and God's gifts?
options: It anticipates the idea that enjoyment of labor and God's gifts is a divine provision for contentment
It rejects the possibility of joy in earthly life
It suggests that riches are earned solely by human effort without divine involvement
It claims that wealth accumulation is the highest spiritual goal
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the idea that enjoyment of labor and God's gifts is a divine provision for contentment
questions.explanation: Verses 18-20 teach that enjoyment of one’s labor and gifts from God is good and a portion given by God, prefiguring NT teachings such as 1 Timothy 6:17 on contentment as a gift from God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ecclesiastes 5:4 and 5:5 teach about vows and human responsibility?
options: It is better not to vow than to vow and fail to fulfill; paying vows is a serious obligation
Vows are optional and can be delayed indefinitely
God accepts unfulfilled vows if intentions are good
Vows are meaningless in the sight of God
questions.correctAnswer: It is better not to vow than to vow and fail to fulfill; paying vows is a serious obligation
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:4-5 emphasize the seriousness of vows before God, teaching that one should not delay to pay them and that it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay, underscoring human responsibility in sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ecclesiastes 5:1 and 5:7 teach regarding human speech and fearing God?
options: Fearing God requires restraint in speech and avoidance of vanity
Speaking much before God is a sign of wisdom
Vanity and many words glorify God
Fearing God removes the need for careful speech
questions.correctAnswer: Fearing God requires restraint in speech and avoidance of vanity
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:1 warns against foolish sacrifices and emphasizes readiness to hear, while 5:7 links many words with vanity, both teaching that fearing God means controlling speech and avoiding emptiness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ecclesiastes 5:12 and 5:13 teach about labor, wealth, and human well-being?
options: Labor brings sweet rest, but riches can bring unrest and harm
Wealth always guarantees peaceful sleep and health
The rich always enjoy better health and rest than laborers
Labor and wealth equally produce sorrow and sickness
questions.correctAnswer: Labor brings sweet rest, but riches can bring unrest and harm
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:12 praises the sweet sleep of the laborer, while 5:13 notes riches kept to their hurt, teaching the paradox that wealth can cause distress despite labor’s rewards.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Ecclesiastes 5:8-9 endorses a cynical acceptance of injustice by urging not to marvel at oppression. What does the passage actually teach?
options: It teaches that God’s sovereignty over higher powers means ultimate justice is assured, despite present injustice
It encourages passive acceptance and indifference towards injustice
It denies God's awareness of earthly injustice
It advocates rebellion against earthly authorities
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God’s sovereignty over higher powers means ultimate justice is assured, despite present injustice
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:8-9 acknowledges the prevalence of injustice but states that God is higher than the highest, watching over all, teaching trust in divine sovereignty and justice rather than cynicism.

questions.question: What doctrine about the consequences of unfaithfulness in vows is taught in Ecclesiastes 5:6?
options: Unfaithfulness in vows can provoke God’s anger and destroy one’s work
God overlooks broken vows if they are said in error
One can excuse broken vows before angels without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Unfaithfulness in vows can provoke God’s anger and destroy one’s work
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:6 warns against causing sin by speech and not excusing broken vows as errors, showing that God’s anger can destroy the work of one’s hands if vows are not honored.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Ecclesiastes 5:7 through the exhortation to 'fear God' amid vanity?
questions.explanation: The call to fear God in Ecclesiastes 5:7 amidst many vanities reflects God's holiness, demanding reverence and separation from vanity and sin.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ecclesiastes 5:14 and 5:16 teach about the futility of wealth when disconnected from God's blessing?
options: Riches produced by evil labor perish and cannot be taken beyond death, showing worldly wealth’s ultimate futility
Wealth is eternal and guarantees blessing beyond death
Laboring for wealth always results in lasting inheritance
Riches are a secure means to eternal life
questions.correctAnswer: Riches produced by evil labor perish and cannot be taken beyond death, showing worldly wealth’s ultimate futility
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:14-16 teach that riches obtained by evil toil perish and cannot be carried away after death, emphasizing the vanity of wealth apart from God’s blessing.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 5:3 contribute to the theological understanding of human folly in speech?
options: Foolishness is often revealed by excessive words and busy activity
Wisdom is demonstrated by many spoken words
Multitude of words always indicates truth
Dreams have no connection to human speech
questions.correctAnswer: Foolishness is often revealed by excessive words and busy activity
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 5:3 explains that a fool’s voice is known by many words and that dreams come through busy pursuits, teaching that excessive speech often signals folly.
